QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_30

question.text: Under SAS-400, Ms. Sunita Patil (SIA CA) observes that the SE employs 180 women out of 300 staff (60%). Which metric best captures GENDER-EQUALITY IMPACT rather than just representation?

answer.text: Female representation at managerial / decision-making layer AND pay-parity AND retention / progression (not just bottom-layer headcount)

explanation.text: The Logic: A meaningful gender-equality impact indicator measures more than aggregate headcount. It looks at female representation across hierarchical layers (entry, middle and senior management), pay parity between male and female employees doing comparable roles, and retention/progression rates. A workforce with 60% women in entry-level roles but no women in management is not delivering gender-equality impact. The Trap: Option A captures only bottom-layer headcount and can mislead. Option C (total staff cost) is purely financial. Option B (average age) is a demographic descriptor unrelated to equality. Note: The cited SIA workbook identifies SAS-400 as the gender-equality theme and presents the Sakhi healthcare case, but does not specifically discuss staff-layer representation, pay parity, retention or progression metrics. The framing above reflects general industry diversity-disclosure practice rather than a workbook-page citation.
